why: The P7 task specifies previews at 960x540, 12 fps, lite FX. 12 is an exact divisor of the ADR-002 F24 film rate, so every preview frame is a film frame and anchor frames halve exactly (no rounding drift between preview and final); 15 fps (tokens.ts, 03 P7.3/P9.1) resamples 24 -> 15 with up to 1/2 frame of rounding. SpecPlayer uses PREVIEW_FPS = 12 (src/spec/resolve.ts); `dc render spec <id> --fps 15` reproduces the token value. Width, height and tier still come from the frozen PREVIEW token.
needs: Council ADR (token change = contract change), then freeze re-hash and dc gate check G6a

target: docs/plan/05_DATA_CONTRACTS.md (word map rec_start_frame / rec_end_frame; anchor frame at fps != 24)
current: 05 does not state the rounding. The word map v1.1 writes rec_start_frame = floor(start_ms x 24 / 1000) and rec_end_frame = ceil(end_ms x 24 / 1000). The sync-verifier found 85 of the 166 CH-10 words differ from round(s x 24) (reports/sync/p7_demo.md section 2).
proposed: Amend 05 by ADR: (1) rec_start_frame = floor(start_ms x 24 / 1000), rec_end_frame = ceil(end_ms x 24 / 1000), so a word's frame span always covers its audio and the picture is 0..41 ms early, never late; (2) an anchor at fps F lands at round_half_up((rec_start_frame - lead_frames - span.start) x F / 24), one rounding (Python: floor(x + 0.5), not round()); exact at 24.
why: Two tools already disagree silently (Python round() is banker's rounding, JS Math.round is half up), and the convention decides whether a picture event can be late. The resolver (studio/src/spec/resolve.ts) implements both rules; tools that read the word map must too.
needs: Council ADR (05 is in docs/plan, never edited directly), then sync-verifier and dc spec lint confirm the same formula

resolution: Q3 = P2: studio/src/tokens.ts PREVIEW.fps 15 -> 12; every preview path reads the token; re-frozen (harness/state/freeze.json contract_changes ADR-011)
Q1 = RD1: word-map frames floor(start_ms*24/1000) / ceil(end_ms*24/1000); anchor at fps F = round_half_up((rec_start_frame - lead_frames - span.start)*F/24), one rounding (studio/src/spec/resolve.ts)

target: studio/src/spec/resolve.ts (ResolvedShot.transition), studio/src/spec/rig.ts (transitionState, streakAt), studio/src/spec/SpecPlayer.tsx (Shot wrapper + streak overlay)
current: resolve.ts keeps only {type, frames} of a WhipPan / LightStreakTransition / MatchCut layer, so their frozen props (direction, color, motion_blur, MatchCut from/to/kind) are validated but ignored. rig.ts applies a whole-frame CSS blur (whip 24 px, streak 12 px) at every tier, always travels RTL, and draws the streak only in the outgoing shot (so it ends at its peak on the cut). The streak colour is fixed at C.signal. MatchCut is a dissolve with a 1.04 scale and no geometric match between the from and to layers.
proposed: Carry the transition layer props into ResolvedShot.transition (fxbTransitionOf), plus the MatchCut from/to layer boxes (from = this shot, to = next shot). In SpecPlayer, use fxbTransitionState / fxbStreakP / streakBand from studio/src/components/_fx-b/transitions.ts (same return shape as TransitionState, plus motionBlur). Wrap the shot in @remotion/motion-blur CameraMotionBlur only when motionBlur is non-null (hero tier, WhipPan.motion_blur = true). No whole-frame CSS blur at lite / standard.
why: 04 section 1.3 says motion blur is 'none' at lite and standard, and 'CameraMotionBlur on whips only' at hero. The current whole-frame blur breaks this, and a full-frame CSS blur is also the most expensive per-frame op on swiftshader. 04 section 2 calls for a 'whip-pan with a light streak'. The frozen schemas expose direction / color / motion_blur / kind, so a scene-director's choice is silently dropped. 04 section 2 prefers match cuts ('a dot becomes a node'), which need the from/to geometry. The drop-in is unit-tested in studio/src/components/_fx-b/shot_level.check.ts (all passed).
needs: Council ADR (engine owner wires it; resolve.check.ts + p7.check.ts + _fx-b/shot_level.check.ts re-run; AT-13-style onset spot check on one whip and one match boundary). Until then LightStreakTransition / WhipPan / MatchCut are 'mapped' to the compiler transitions streak / whip / match (docs/p7/catalog_status/fx-b.md).

current: CameraRig.follow (a layer id, frozen schema) is validated but dropped. move 'follow' behaves exactly like 'truck': a fixed 80 px x intensity pan.
proposed: Copy follow into ResolvedShot.camera.follow and resolve it to the target layer box centre. In cameraAt, ease the pan so that the box centre moves toward the frame centre by at most 80 px x intensity (the truck envelope), so cameraSafeBox stays valid unchanged. Report an unknown follow id as invalid props.
why: 04 section 2: 'truck/pan along a flow = following data'. The schema promises a follow target, and a scene-director cannot tell the difference today.
needs: Council ADR; engine owner; resolve.check.ts camera-envelope cases re-run with follow.

current: DemoDef has no features field, and demoInput passes features: null. Demo-AudioReactive therefore renders with zero modulation, and its snapshots and perf only show the unmodulated layers.
proposed: Add an optional DemoDef.features (a Features object on the demo's 24 fps frames: synthetic, deterministic, labelled synthetic), and have demoInput pass it through.
why: Snapshot and perf evidence for AudioReactive should include the modulation path (glow / scale / haze per frame). Today it is proven only by unit checks (_fx-b/shot_level.check.ts) and by chapter renders that carry the locked P5 features.
needs: Engine owner (type-only change plus one line in demoInput); then fx-b re-baselines Demo-AudioReactive (critic).

current: zones: {upto, status} only; the printed zone boundary (e.g. the 500 ms gate) has no ref
proposed: zones: {upto, status, ref?: NumberRef} so a printed boundary carries its data ref (d:6.11:1 for the 500 ms gate)
why: Rule 11 / 05 section 8 lint: every shown number carries a ref. The component prints each zone boundary (`upto`) under the scale; until a ref exists the scene must speak the number (the schema cannot prove it).
needs: Council ADR (frozen schema + harness/schemas/components/ThresholdSlider.json); then the component reads zones[].ref

current: stages.max(8); the CH-11 funnel has nine logical stages (d:6.3:2: 14,13,11,2,2,2,2,2,1 across FROM, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT)
why: The data contract names nine stages (d:6.3:16). With max 8 the demo and the scene must drop DISTINCT (the query has no DISTINCT clause, its count is the unchanged 2, so no number is lost, but the spoken 'nine stages' cannot be drawn).

current: left/right carry only {name, keys}; no row data
proposed: optional rows: [{key: string}] per table (<= 8) so a scene can show its real key multiset (e.g. the 6.4 fan-out 4/3/4/2/1/1 customers)
why: JoinFusion currently animates five abstract rows with fixed keys (K1..K5 vs K2 K3 K3 K5 K6): the match structure (1:1, 1:2 fan-out, unmatched) is generic, and no number is invented, but a scene cannot show the real per-customer row counts of d:6.4:1.

current: sample: K.Num is required, with value + ref
why: Fact-check D2 (reports/facts/p7_data_gaps.md): no sample size n exists in the canon or data contract, and n must never be displayed. The scoop draws a fixed decorative dot count and ignores `sample`, but the schema forces a scene to supply a number with a ref. The demo has to pass the sourced population value (s:S4:P11:0070) as a placeholder, which states a false quantity in the spec data.

current: users and rate are required Num objects (value + ref)
proposed: users and rate optional; when absent (or when no rate ref is a d: fact) the lanes render ordinal bars, and `reveal.winner` selects the winner
why: Fact-check D1: the canon holds no A/B users or rates, so today a film scene may show no digits. The schema forces placeholder numbers with a sentence ref. The component already refuses to draw digits unless every rate ref is a data-contract fact (d:x.y:n), so ordinal placeholders (rank only) are the workaround.

current: LayerCtx exposes only the layer own box; StatusStamp `to` (a LayerId) cannot be resolved to the target layer rectangle
proposed: LayerCtx.rectOf(layerId): Rect | undefined, the target layer box on the same depth plane (after the camera envelope shrink)
why: StatusStamp.to is a frozen prop. Without the target rect the stamp can only land in its own slot, so the scene-director must give the stamp the same slot as the target. This works but makes `to` inert.

current: The text-safe hole is a canvas-drawn PNG data URL used as a CSS mask-image. Nothing in the settle sequence (fonts, auto-fit, target measures) waits for that image to decode. Observed: `dc render snap TermChip` failed determinism twice (970 px, identical count) and LowerThird once (1147 px) while a 3-repeat probe passed; the differing pixels are +/-1 level on the full-frame lite backdrop (vertical/horizontal seam lines plus the haze band), i.e. the faint haze band with and without its hole. Passes and failures alternate with queue load, so it is a timing race, not a component state. Cause is suspected, not proven.
proposed: In textSafeMask (or SpecPlayer's checkWhenSettled), hold a delayRender until each hole sprite's Image has decoded (new Image().src = url; await img.decode()) before the screenshot, or draw the hole as an inline SVG/radial-gradient mask that needs no async decode. Re-run `dc render snap` 5x on TermChip and LowerThird (and _selftest) to confirm 0 px every time.
why: A non-deterministic frame can never become a baseline (guide section 5) and would make a final render differ run to run (G9b reproducibility); today a flaky snap needs a re-run.
needs: Council ADR or engine owner (SpecPlayer/Atmos are shared, not group files)

current: show_ids: boolean and no id values; the draft prints the token position in the stream ("#3"), not a vocabulary id
proposed: add optional ids: z.array(z.number().int().min(0)).max(40) (one per token) and ids_ref: K.NumberRef; show_ids prints ids[i] (mono, Western digits) when given, else the position
why: 04 section 6 NLP: tokens carry ids. A printed vocabulary id is a number and needs a ref (rule 11); the position fallback is honest but is not what a tokenizer shows.

current: scores_ref: DataRef is carried but no score values: the component cannot draw the cosine figures the look-dev F4 frame shows (0.227 / 0.165)
proposed: add optional scores: z.array(K.Frac).max(10) (rank order); the figure is printed beside each neighbour (2 decimals, mono) and scores_ref is its ref
why: A figure on screen needs a value and a ref. Today the neighbours are drawn by proximity only; authors use NumberCounter / CalloutArrow for the figure.

current: items carry {label, kind} only; the window (a Num) is printed on the gate, but no per-item token size exists, so eviction is by slot count (CAP = 5 cards, an illustration constant), not by token budget
proposed: add optional tokens: K.Num on items[] and on push (value + ref); evict the oldest while sum(tokens) > window.value; the gate then shows the true fill
why: CH-33 teaches that the window is a token budget (s:S4:P22:0074: 4,000 to 128,000 tokens). Slot-count eviction shows the idea but not the budget arithmetic.
